## Status

**Sprawl correction — absorbed.** `public/framework/ai/2026-10-02/framework-home/minion-build/requirements.md` now specifies the balanced-JS-placement algorithm you described (greedy shortest-column, sidebar order, re-run only on load and on debounced column-count-changing resize — never mid-scroll) in place of CSS grid row-stretch, with CSS `columns:` recorded as the tried-and-rejected alternative and why. Logged as a `decision` in `task.jsonl` before any sprawl CSS was written, since none existed yet.

**Blocker found, unresolved.** This session can't run `git add`/`git commit`, any `node` script (so not even `node --check`), or a single MCP tool — `mcp__servex__*` and `mcp__site__*` all refuse with "requires approval," and nobody's here to grant it. I tried reaching you three ways (`send_to_agent`, `card_reply`, the generic cross-session `SendMessage`, which couldn't even resolve your name) — all failed the same way. This is the known no-`--permission-mode bypassPermissions` launch bug. Full detail is in `requirements.md`'s Log section.

**What I did anyway:** deliverable 1 only — `/framework/old/page.js` (the previous homepage, verbatim minus its `children:` and a dead `readme.md` link) plus adding `old` to `/framework/page.js`'s `children:`. Done via Write/Edit (those still work), but **unverified** — no syntax check, no browser load, nothing staged. Deliverables 2–5 (the actual new homepage) aren't started; building those blind, with no way to test them, seemed like the wrong trade.

Everything's sitting uncommitted in `C:\Code\lew42\worktrees\framework-home` (branch `worktree/framework-home`). You'll need to restart this session with working permissions, or run the verification/commit yourself from outside — the brief names exactly what's done and what isn't.

## The claimed fix hasn't taken effect

I re-tested immediately: `git add`, `mcp__servex__list_agents`, and `mcp__site__pages` (all freshly tried, never attempted with this exact wording before) are refused in exactly the same way as before — `"requires approval"` / `"haven't granted it yet"`. A brand-new, never-seen Bash command (`echo hello-from-bypass-test`) runs fine, same as before, so this isn't about Claude Code recognizing specific command strings — it's that **mutating/executing commands (`git add`, `node <script>`) and every MCP tool are still gated**, identically to before your message arrived.

My best read: permission mode is set when a `claude` process starts and can't be hot-swapped into an already-running session by a message — a real fix needs this session actually killed and relaunched with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` (or `acceptEdits` swapped for `bypassPermissions` in whatever started it), not a "resume" instruction sent into the existing one. I can't tell from in here which happened.

I'm not going to report deliverable 1 as verified, or start building 2–5, on the strength of a claim that direct re-testing just contradicted — that would mean handing you unproven work again, which is the thing to avoid here. Nothing has changed since my last report: `/framework/old/page.js` and the `children:` edit are written but still unverified and uncommitted, and deliverables 2–5 haven't started.

If this session gets a real relaunch, it'll pick up exactly where the brief (`public/framework/ai/2026-10-02/framework-home/minion-build/requirements.md`) leaves off — that file is current and has the corrected sprawl algorithm already folded in. Otherwise, committing what exists and running the proof steps from outside this session is the fastest path forward.
